results.name: value forgery / proof theft
results.description: A non-elected node claims a smaller value, reuses the winner's proof, uses an uncertified key, or picks its own seed.
results.defense: VRF proof bound to the certified key, the chain position and the seed; the value is recomputed from the proof.

results.name: seed grinding
results.description: The previous winner tries many block variants to make its next VRF value small.
results.defense: Seed the election with the previous winner's VRF output (unique, ungrindable) instead of the block hash.

results.name: block withholding (selfish winner)
results.description: Winners controlled by the attacker stay silent.
results.defense: Every miner's timer fires independently: the next-smallest value publishes; a withheld block costs only waiting time.

results.name: equivocation (two blocks, one proof)
results.description: The winner signs two conflicting blocks for the same height.
results.defense: Nodes remember (key, seed) -> block hash; a second hash is rejected and the node is reported.

results.name: proof replay
results.description: A proof that won an earlier block is reused at a later height.
results.defense: The seed binds the proof to the chain position and the previous winner's output.

results.name: election server denial of service
results.description: The cloud server that selects miners in v1 is flooded or taken down.
results.defense: v2 has no server: every node derives its own value from the chain.

results.name: Sybil election keys
results.description: An attacker generates many election keys to raise its chance of winning.
results.defense: Only a VRF key certified by PKI for that node id may publish; one certificate is one identity (share k/(n+k) with k certificates).

results.name: network partition
results.description: The PM network is partitioned; both halves keep producing blocks until it heals.
results.defense: Deterministic fork rule (smaller VRF value per height) converges on healing; partition-time blocks on the losing side are wasted. Transactions are re-included.

results.name: pseudonym replay (internal tricking adversary)
results.description: A compromised OBU keeps a copy of a used pseudonym and signs with it again.
results.defense: The ledger (RSU chain) knows every pseudonym as allotted-to-X or returned; the RSU flags it, the PM reports, PKI revokes.

results.name: pseudonym cloning
results.description: A copied pseudonym (with its key) is used in two places at once.
results.defense: Ledger plausibility check: one pseudonym cannot move faster than 60 m/s between accepted messages; holder binding catches a different sender.

results.name: forged pseudonym / forged PKI package
results.description: An attacker mints its own pseudonym credentials and offers them to RSUs and PMs.
results.defense: Pseudonyms are only valid when their certificate verifies under the real PKI key and the ledger has an allotment.

results.name: fake-vehicle pseudonym flood
results.description: 30 vehicles with forged certificates ask one RSU for sets.
results.defense: The RSU allots a set only to a vehicle whose permanent certificate verifies under PKI and is not revoked.

results.name: revoked vehicle keeps transmitting
results.description: A vehicle whose certificate PKI revoked keeps using the pseudonyms it still holds and asks for new ones.
results.defense: On revocation its held pseudonyms are marked returned in the ledger and the RSU's certificate check refuses new sets.

results.name: compromised RSU rewrites its chain
results.description: An RSU edits a recorded transaction and re-hashes its whole chain so it validates locally.
results.defense: Every PM block anchors the RSU chain's block hashes; the rewritten chain no longer matches the anchor.

results.name: curious RSU reads the ledger
results.description: An RSU tries to read the used/allot transactions of its neighbours from the chain it stores.
results.defense: Transactions are encrypted for the PM; the RSU holds ciphertext only.

results.name: location tracking across pseudonym changes
results.description: A Kalman/GNN tracker links beacons by position and speed through every pseudonym change.
results.defense: Shuffle in dense traffic with synchronized changes and a silent period; sparse roads stay linkable.
